records.our_prose: Here you grow pole beans in two seasons, spring and fall, with a summer break between. records.our_prose: The Southeast and Gulf run two pole bean crops split by summer heat. Sow in spring after frost against a tall trellis, and again in mid to late summer for a fall crop. The gap is real: through the hottest weeks blossoms drop and pods fail to set. Each planting bears progressively for weeks rather than all at once, so one sowing per window is enough; pick every couple of days. The spring sowing anchors to roughly mid March in middle Georgia and shifts earlier deeper south.
